correctness.rationale: The last-column decomposition yields P_j=a_j P_(j-1)+b_j P_(j-2). Gauging by the product of the rung signs gives u_0=u_1=1 and u_j=u_(j-1)+epsilon_j u_(j-2), where epsilon_j=b_j a_(j-1) a_j. The gauge preserves magnitudes and each normalized string has 2^n rung choices and 2^(n-1) horizontal-pair sign lifts, giving the exact kernel multiplicity. All-plus gives the Fibonacci maximum; all signed sums have Fibonacci parity. The all-minus orbit (1,1,0,-1,-1,0) proves both singularity in the even-Fibonacci residue and attainment of absolute value one elsewhere. Flipping its last sign at a resonant width gives magnitude two. At n=1 the two frequencies have magnitude one. Starting at a zero at width 2, each subsequent three-step block can freely assign its first two signs and take its last sign minus, returning to zero; this proves Z_(3k-1)>=4^(k-1) and the stated fraction bound. The independent Python replay at branches/2af68975-471d-4be0-856f-c5ca19a59e03/signed_recurrence_check.py checked all width-1 through width-15 normalized strings and checked the physical-edge fibers directly through width 4, with the five listed zero counts reproduced. The frozen scripts were read, not executed. These bounded data corroborate, not prove, the all-width reasoning.

evidence: The height-three Dyck catalogue statement, suffix 51de04f7e6b4, explicitly gives a Fibonacci-cube affine model, modulo-three invertibility, least nonzero absolute values 1 or 2, and 7032 zeros at semilength 8.

For the ladder, putting a mark on each join with a horizontal pair parametrizes binary strings of length n-1 with no adjacent marks. Both horizontal-edge bits copy the mark; a rung bit is one plus its incident marks modulo two. This is an injective affine map of the same cube.

For a height-at-most-three Dyck path of semilength m>=2, remove the first and last steps. The inner height walk starts and ends at height 1. At odd interior times use a mark for height 0 instead of 2, and at even interior times use a mark for height 3 instead of 1. Of the adjacent choices only height 0 next to height 3 is forbidden. This yields exactly the no-adjacent-ones cube of length 2m-3. The up-step bits are the affine differences of neighboring marks, with the fixed end heights; the map is injective since the heights are recovered from steps.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: If an injective affine map has binary linear part B of rank d, a signed sum at frequency s is the cube signed sum at B^T s times a sign. Every cube character occurs in exactly 2^(ambient dimension-d) frequencies. Thus two such models of the same d have identical absolute spectrum after quotienting by these known multiplicities. The correspondence n-1=2m-3 gives n=2m-2, and m=2 mod 3 exactly when n=2 mod 3. This is exact overlap on an infinite natural subfamily, not a conjectured analogy.

originality.rationale: Material coverage of the headline spectral recovery theorem is demonstrable, not merely a similarity of recurrences. The earlier indexed height-three Dyck result gives the same invertibility law and sharp signed multiplier gaps for an affine copy of precisely the same Fibonacci cube at every even ladder width n=2m-2, where m is Dyck semilength. Its reported 7032 zeros at m=8 also give the exact normalized zero count 879 at ladder width 14, not a different spectral statistic. The extension to odd widths uses the same cube and elementary parity and sign witnesses. The frozen record's claim of a distinct sharp recovery invariant as framed therefore does not pass originality. This comparison does not establish that the quantitative lower bound at all resonant widths was previously proved, and is not a rejection for unavailable full text. No substantively narrowed replacement is submitted.
